title: Woman told 911 of 'meds' ; Revealed at inquest
article: Police officers who took a Winnipeg woman to a downtown shelter -- where she later died -- to "sober up" were unaware she had told a 911 operator it was her "meds" that made her appear intoxicated, an inquest heard yesterday.
"I take it that it would have been helpful if you knew she told the 911 operator the difficulty she had speaking was due to her meds?" lawyer Greg Brodsky asked Const. Michael Klassen.

Cheryl Lynn Tom, a 35-year-old mother of three, died March 26, 2007, after police, believing she was intoxicated, apprehended her at a St. James 7-Eleven store and dropped her off at the Main Street Project to sober up. She was later found dead. An autopsy revealed she died of a multiple drug overdose.
Klassen said if he knew Tom was taking medication he would have asked her what kind.
"When we asked her if she had taken alcohol or drugs, she said nothing," Klassen testified.

The inquest has heard Tom was diagnosed in 2004 with treatment-resistant depression and possible borderline personality traits. She was prescribed a variety of medications in the years up to her death.
The manager of the 7-Eleven testified she walked Tom out of the store after she was allegedly caught stealing another staff member's cigarettes.
"She was easily led, she walked under her own steam with my arm in her back area," Barb Bowler testified.
A security video showed Tom returning 10 minutes later. In between her expulsion from the store and her return, Tom placed a call to 911.

After a brief scuffle at the door, Bowler pulled Tom inside and Tom fell to the floor. The security video shows Bowler standing over an unmoving Tom until police arrive and she is escorted to a police cruiser.
Bowler said she saw Tom's eyes roll back in her head but did not alert police to any possible medical concern.
Another staff member, Michael Hanson, said he smelled no alcohol on Tom and told police "more than once" she had not been drinking.
"I heard someone say 'Take her to the drunk tank.' I said she's not drunk," Hanson testified.
